definitions.explanation: An ingredient, mix, or concentrate that serves as the base for making something else. Especially common in food product names like だしの{素|もと} (dashi base) or ラーメンの{素|もと} (ramen base).

examples.japanese: だしの{素|もと}を{使|つか}う。
お{好|この}み{焼|や}きの{素|もと}を{買|か}ってきた。
{鍋|なべ}の{素|もと}を{使|つか}えば、{家|いえ}でも{簡単|かんたん}に{本格的|ほんかくてき}な{味|あじ}が{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: If you use a hot-pot base, you can easily enjoy an authentic taste at home.

notes:
{素|もと} as a base/mix is almost always written with the kanji {素|もと} and attaches with の to the name of the dish: {dish}の{素|もと} = "{dish} base." Often sold as a powder, paste, or concentrate.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- だしの{素|もと}: dashi base
- お{好|この}み{焼|や}きの{素|もと}: okonomiyaki mix
- カレーの{素|もと}: curry base/mix
- {鍋|なべ}の{素|もと}: hot-pot base
- {唐揚|からあ}げの{素|もと}: karaage seasoning mix

WATCH OUT:
- {元|もと}: origin; former — different kanji, different meaning
- {基|もと}: basis, foundation — abstract grounding (に{基|もと}づく)
